newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Pike toll cuts could mean downgrade - Sandler.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Pike toll cuts could mean downgrade - Sandler.

text.p: Eliminating more tolls or reducing existing ones along the Massachusetts Turnpike could prompt a credit rating downgrade, Sandler O'Neill & Partners LP said in a new research report.

"Based on public comments made by state officials, we believe that additional toll eliminations and/or reductions are a distinct possibility in the near future," Sandler muni research director Michael Johnston said in the report.
"Sandler O'Neill believes that additional toll reductions or eliminations could elicit a negative reaction in the form of a rating downgrade," the report said.

The report also said a downgrade for the Turnpike Authority was more likely from Standard & Poor's Corp than Moody's Investors Service, since S&P's current A-plus rating does not entirely account for the risk of more toll reductions. Moody's rates the Turnpike Authority A1.

Sandler said that the $14 million of revenues lost to recent toll eliminations was "modest." But the firm noted a recent warning from Moody's that the Turnpike's indenture appears to prohibit free service. That might mean the authority is in technical violation of its covenants to bondholders, Moody's said.

In adding the Authority to its Watch List of municipal bonds, Sandler said it sees the Turnpike's long-term credit outlook as unclear. The report noted that Massachusetts seems to be using the Authority as a tool to achieve broader policy goals, noting for example the recent announcement of a proposed $300 million hotel and sports complex built over the Turnpike.

"What may be significant in the long run is the potential that this action is the first step to broadening MassPike's public mission, which could create new uncertainties and credit risks which are at present difficult to quantify," the report said.
Sandler stressed that increasing the authority's mandate does not in itself represent a negative credit concern, though it could eventually lead to higher amounts of debt or credit risk.
Johnston said in the report that the secondary market does not appear to be penalizing Turnpike bonds as a result of the recent toll developments.

Kenny Evaluation Services on Monday priced the authority's 5.0s of 2020 to yield 5.65 percent. That compares to a 5.68 percent yield on Nov 21, a level which does not indicate much spread over generic single-A scales, Johnston said.
